title: SQL Queries and Joins
notes: Code-heavy SQL lecture. Checks that the summary keeps INNER vs LEFT semantics (NULLs for unmatched rows) rather than blurring them. Traps: window functions, CTEs and indexes, the usual next lecture.

pages.text:
Week 4 — SQL Joins.

Tables: students(id, name) and enrolments(student_id, course).

SELECT s.name, e.course
FROM students s
INNER JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id;

An INNER JOIN keeps only rows that match on the ON condition. A student with no enrolment does not appear.

SELECT s.name, e.course
FROM students s
LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id;

A LEFT JOIN keeps every row of the left table. Where there is no match the right-hand columns are NULL. To find students with no enrolment add WHERE e.course IS NULL.

GROUP BY collapses rows into groups so an aggregate such as COUNT can be computed per group:

SELECT s.name, COUNT(e.course)
FROM students s LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id
GROUP BY s.name;

WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after.

required_facts.fact: INNER JOIN keeps only matching rows
LEFT JOIN keeps all left rows with NULL for unmatched right columns
all: every row of the left table

required_facts.fact: IS NULL finds students with no enrolment
WHERE filters before grouping, HAVING after

forbidden_claims.claim: says INNER JOIN keeps unmatched rows
